question.leadin: Give the following about the decolonization of Africa.
question.text: This former French colony's National Liberation Front, or FLN, won its independence in an eight-year war that ended with the Evian Accords.
question.clue: This country is the largest both in area and population in the Maghreb Union and the majority of the Tell Atlas Mountains are found in this country.

swap.text: Osama bin Laden first appeared on the FBI's Most Wanted Terrorists list after his involvement in an 1998 embassy bombing in this country with capital at Nairobi.
swap.clue: To finance the massively expensive "lunatic express" railway in this country, large amounts of land in the highlands was seized.

question.leadin: This country's late 1960s civil war began with the secession of a state populated by its Igbo [ig-BOW] people.
question.text: Name this African country, which fought a civil war against the state of Biafra. This country's capital was moved to Abuja in 1991.
question.answerHtml: Nigeria [or Federal Republic of Nigeria; accept Nigerian Civil War]
question.clue: Olusegun Obasanjo served as both a military ruler and as an elected head of state at different times in this country, which saw ethnic tensions erupt when the Republic of Biafra declared independence.

swap.text: The most famous ruler of Mali was this man. His general Sagmandia conquered Gao, and his own accomplishments include founding Sankore University and debasing the value of gold in Egypt during his hajj.
swap.clue: This person was depicted holding a fleur-de-lys and a golden orb by Abraham Cresques on the Atlas of Catalan.

question.leadin: One city in this empire included a massive library of Islamic learning at the University of Sankore ["sahn-CORE-eh"].
question.text: Name this empire, the home of many griots that recorded oral history. One griot epic tells the story of Sundiata Keita founding this empire by beating Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.
question.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.text: This semi-legendary figure was the namesake of an epic that described how he became the first emperor of Mali after defeating the evil Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.
swap.clue: This man's mother Sogolon was an extremely ugly woman who had previously lived as a buffalo.

question.text: This kingdom in modern South Africa lost the Battles of Blood River and Ulundi and was earlier led by Shaka, who adopted the innovative buffalo horn formation in battle and replaced the traditional assegai with the iklwa.
question.clue: This kingdom's defeat at the Battle of Blood River caused the death of two rival claimants to the throne of its king, Dingane.

swap.text: After succeeding Jaafar Nimeiry, this president and dictator initiated the genocide in Darfur with the help of Janjaweed militias. This leader was overthrown in a military coup in early 2019.
swap.clue: This leader introduced Shari'a law with the support of Hasan al-Turabi, founder of the National Islamic Front.

question.leadin: This man's 1936 speech to the League of Nations condemned the use of chemical weapons against his country.
question.text: Name this emperor of Ethiopia, worshipped as a messiah in Rastafarianism.
question.clue: He was eventually deposed, in part because of a famine in the Wollo region, by a committee known as the Derg.

swap.text: Gordon later died while serving as governor-general of the Sudan during the siege of Khartoum by this leader of a mystical Islamic empire in northeast Africa.
swap.answerHtml: the Mahdi [or al-Mahdi; or Muhammad Ahmad Ibn As-sayyid ‘abd Allah]
swap.clue: He named his followers the "helpers" or "ansar" and attempted to set up his government with four immediate deputies known as "caliphs," though the leader of the Sanusiyah refused to participate.

question.leadin: This man halted the Move to the Left program after overthrowing Milton Obote.
question.text: Name this Ugandan dictator who expelled all Asians from his country in 1972 and was overthrown by forces sent by Julius Nyerere.
question.clue: This dictator led a failed invasion of a country led by Julius Nyerere and allegedly ordered the murder of Dora Bloch.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about questionable fashion decisions from African dictators.
swap.text: This man, whose toothbrush mustache only covers the philtrum of his nose, was a leader in the war against Ian Smith's Rhodesian government. His defeats of rival politician Morgan Tsvangirai have been tinged with corruption.
swap.clue: This leader's G-40-backed wife and a military-backed member of the ZANU both vied to succeed him as president after a 2017 coup.

question.leadin: The Lemon project at the College of William & Mary features the donning of stoles made of this cloth for African-American students.
question.text: Name these handwoven textiles which are colorful patterns of interwoven strips of typically silk and cotton that originate from Ghana.
question.clue: The Akan and Ashanti people are associated with this traditional style of cloth. Nancy Pelosi drew ridicule for wearing this fabric at a Black Lives Matter event in 2020.

swap.leadin: One crisis during this man's rule was touched off by the death of Joseph Rendjambe, one of his political opponents.
swap.text: Name this ruler of Gabon for much of the later parts of the 20th century who held power through several questionable elections until his 2009 death.
swap.clue: Thanks to his country's massive supply of uranium, this leader's country was the main supplier to the nuclear program of France for years.

question.leadin: A leader of these people fortified a natural plateau that he named Thaba Bosiu after Nguni ("in-GOO-nee") settlers arrived in the Drakensburg region during a period sometimes called the "Mfecane" ("mʼfeh-KAH-neh").
question.text: Name these people whose leader Moshoeshoe I ("muh-SHWAY-shway the first") settled them around Maseru in a namesake British protectorate. These people fought three wars over land around the Caledon River with the Orange Free State.
question.answerHtml: Sotho people [or Basuto people or Basotho people; accept Northern Sotho or Southern Sotho or West Sotho; accept Tswana-Sotho people; accept Basutoland Protectorate; prompt on Lesotho; prompt on Bantu people; prompt on Tswana by asking “from what other group of people did they split from?”]

swap.leadin: This leader came to power after junta leader Robert Guei barred all opposition leaders from running against him.
swap.text: Name this world leader who refused to step down after Alassane Ouattara defeated him in a November 2010 presidential election.
swap.clue: This former President of the Ivory Coast who was acquitted by the ICC alongside Charles Ble Goude.

question.leadin: According to legend, a politician from this political party, which allied with Abdulrahman Mohamad Babu's far-left Umma Party, became an evil spirit called the popobawa upon his 1972 assassination.
question.text: Name this political party that merged with TANU after the death of its leader Abeid Karume ("uh-BAYD kah-ROO-may"). Its bloody overthrow of Jamshid ("jam-SHEED") bin ʿAbdullah was led on the ground by, inexplicably, the Christian fanatic John Okello.

swap.text: The German explorer Heinrich Barth preserved two copies of the Girgam, the over eight centuries long king list of this empire whose capitals included Ngazargamu [in-GAHZ-ar-GAH-moo] and Kukawa [koo-KAH-wah].
swap.clue: One important mai or king of this nation named Hummay converted it to Islam and founded the Sayfawa dynasty.

question.leadin: British troops in this country managed to gain the allegiance of the West Side Boys, an armed militia who dressed as American gang members in the style of Tupac.
question.text: Name this country where the Revolutionary United Front, led by Foday Sankoh, fought the government in a civil war from 1991 to 2002. The Abidjan Peace Accords created a brief ceasefire in this country's civil war that only ended due to British intervention.
question.clue: Resentment of this country's Krio elite was exploited by Foday Sankoh, the leader of the Revolutionary United Front, whose use of cocaine-addicted child soldiers is attested in Ishmael Beah's A Long Way Gone.

swap.text: For her efforts, Gbowee won the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize along with this woman, who became the first modern African head of state after Charles Taylor's resignation following the peace talks.
swap.clue: This politician who lost to Charles Taylor in 1997 but defeated George Weah (WEE-uh) in 2005 to become the first elected female head of state in Africa.
